summary: Configured node1–node3 as a persistent three-member MariaDB Galera cluster. All members are currently active, Primary, Connected, Synced, Ready, and report nine identical replicated validation rows after failover and rolling OS restarts.
actions_performed: Installed Galera-capable MariaDB 10.1.48 on all nodes and configured unique member identities with a shared cluster address.
Created node-local generated credentials for authenticated TCP validation against each node's managed IP.
Verified writes through every member replicate to all other members.
Stopped node3 and confirmed node1/node2 remained readable and writable with quorum.
Restored node3 and confirmed automatic resynchronization of writes made during its absence.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially, verifying changed boot identities and full recovery after each.

evidence.requirement: Three-member cluster is healthy and data is identical on every member
evidence.summary: All nodes are enabled/active, share nine rows and one cluster UUID, and report size 3, Primary, Connected, Synced, Ready.

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member replicate to the others
evidence.summary: Each managed IP accepted a distinct authenticated TCP write; every member subsequently returned all three writes.

evidence.requirement: Database remains readable and writable while one member is unavailable
evidence.summary: With node3 inactive, node1 and node2 remained Primary, Synced, Ready at size 2 and accepted/read distinct writes.

evidence.requirement: Returning member automatically rejoins with writes made during its absence
evidence.summary: node3 returned via normal service startup, became Synced/Ready in the restored size-3 cluster, and contained both outage-period writes.
Captured healthy baseline boot ID, acknowledged the reboot, observed a changed boot ID, then verified enabled/active service, preserved data, and full size-3 recovery.
